messages:
emma (oncall): Pager: high queue growth on gpu-pool-a, autoscale failed to add nodes. Seeing >12k pending tokens, requests 504ing.
incident-bot: [ALERT] gpu-pool-a capacity_exhaustion at 2026-03-15T09:20:00Z — severity: high — page sent to #incidents — runbook: gpu-pool-capacity.
emma (oncall): I'm checking autoscaler logs now, pinging raj to take lead if I need to rotate.
raj (sre): on it. first look: autoscaler hit max_replicas for node-group gpu-a-spot (limit 24), tried burst but failed due to quota.
maya (infra): Confirmed quota prevents new instances. Cloud shows allocation pending, but placement failing because large MIG slices required (2x32G per node) and we have fragmented free capacity across hosts.
tom (runtime): Runtime reports high binpack fragmentation: many pods pinned to specific MIG sizes (1g,2g) and several long-running eval jobs locked 8x1g slices, leaving 3 nodes with unusable leftover.
em ma (oncall): typo — emma: Thanks. can we evict any non-critical pods?
raj (sre): I'm listing top-k pods by gpu_request:
```
kubectl get pods -n inference -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GD:.spec.resources.requests.nvidia.com/gpu,AGE:.status.startTime | sort -k2 -nr | head -n 20
```
raj (sre): Found ~6 long-running tune jobs (team: research) holding many 1g MIG slices; they have restartPolicy=Never and are not preemptible.
maya (infra): Those were scheduled with static MIG affinity. We probably over-committed 1g pool. I'll check if we can temporarily relax MIG pinning.
tom (runtime): We have a pending rebalance operation that has been stuck for ~45m due to lock contention on scheduler shard-3. That prevents automated defragmentation.
akel (customer-ops): Customer-impact: multiple customers on tier 'growth' report 10-30s token latency spikes and some 504s. Support case #CS-1123 is high priority.
emma (oncall): Okay, escalate plan: (1) attempt manual eviction of non-critical research pods with 10m grace, (2) temp increase autoscaler max_replicas if cloud quota permits, (3) enable fallback routing to model-compact for affected routes, (4) kick the rebalance manually on shard-3. Any objections?
raj (sre): Good. I'm taking step 1/evictions. Annotating pod list and pinging research lead.
maya (infra): I'm on cloud quota request but it will take time. I'll also look for any stopped instances that can be resized to mixed MIG to reduce fragmentation.
tom (runtime): To kick rebalance:
```
# debug command
curl -XPOST http://scheduler.internal/scheduler/rebalance?shard=3 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

But the API is returning 409 lock; need to clear stale lock: `kubectl delete configmap scheduler-lock-shard-3 -n scheduler` — I'm going to coordinate with SRE before running.
raj (sre): Proceeding with evictions now: `kubectl drain research-job-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=600`
akel (customer-ops): I've posted status to affected customers: we're throttling new heavy evals and routing some traffic to fallback models. Will update/post in CS-1123.
emma (oncall): Deploy-bot, any recent deploys that could've changed pod affinities?
deploy-bot: [DEPLOY] inference-scheduler v2.14 deployed by maya at 2026-03-15T08:05:12Z — no MIG-affinity changes in this PR.
maya (infra): Evictions succeeded for 4/6 research pods; 2 refused due to anchor annotation `cannot-preempt`. I'm requesting tag removal from research lead.
raj (sre): After evictions, pending queue dropped from 12k -> 7.1k, token latency median improved from 18s -> 9s. Still degraded but better.
tom (runtime): I deleted the stale lock and retried rebalance; it started and shows progress: 30% of rebalance completed, moving small slices to consolidate.
akel (customer-ops): Noting customers on dedicated pools unaffected; most impact is hosted growth tier. Sending interim SLA note.
emma (oncall): Any chance of stranded capacity after rebalance? We need to ensure MIG sizing map updated so scheduler doesn't re-pin new jobs incorrectly.
maya (infra): We identified a config mismatch: default mig_profile for small jobs was recently bumped to '1g-legacy' in a hotfix, but runtime expects '1g-new' packing. That mismatch caused fragmentation. I'll roll a fix to map aliases back.
raj (sre): I'm temporarily increasing autoscaler max_replicas to 30 for gpu-a-spot (cloud allows transient spike to 28; set to 28) — doing a controlled increase to avoid quota errors.
tom (runtime): Once rebalance finishes we should drain and recycle 2 problem nodes to allow fresh binpacking. Scheduling a rolling reboot for nodes gpu-node-198 and -205 after rebalance.
akel (customer-ops): CS updated: latency improving, some 504s remain for heavy batch jobs; mitigation routed to fallback models and queued jobs will retry. Customers acknowledged.
emma (oncall): Handing incident to raj for containment & postmortem. I'll remain on-call until structured handoff completes.
raj (sre): Taking over incident. Next steps: root cause draft, timelines, postmortem checklist — I'll collect autoscaler metrics, rebalance logs, MIG profile diffs, and customer impact windows.
maya (infra): Actions logged: revert mig_profile alias, allow rebalance to complete, remove `cannot-preempt` annotation policy for long-running research jobs, propose new quota limit or on-demand capacity for burst.
tom (runtime): Post-incident fixes: add canary for mig_profile changes in staging, add stronger lock telemetry for scheduler shards, implement automated soft-eviction for non-critical pods when queue > threshold.
akel (customer-ops): Final customer note prepared, will send after containment confirmed.
incident-bot: [RESOLVE] Alert gpu-pool-a capacity_exhaustion resolved at 2026-03-15T09:05:00Z — degraded service removed. Incident severity downgraded to mitigated.
raj (sre): Last note: rebalance completed, pending queue back to baseline ~300, autoscaler scaled down to normal, cloud quota request opened to raise max_replicas to 40 for gpu-a-spot.
emma (oncall): Thanks team. Postmortem owner: raj. I'll add timeline and handoff notes.
